result.text: We simulate spall failure on Nb single crystals using high-velocity impact simulations using molecular dynamics (MD) with the LAMMPS code. We simulate the impact of a projectile on a target with a relative velocity of 2 km/s. The projectile is obtained by replicating the Nb BCC unit cell 20 times along the [100], [010], and [001]; the target is longer along the shock direction and is obtained by replicating the BCC unit cell 20 times along [100] and [010] and 40 times along [001]. We apply periodic boundary conditions along the directions normal to the impact direction, [001], and free boundaries along [001]. A gap of 1.5 nm initially separates the target and projectile. The system is equilibrated at 300 K for 100 ps using isothermal, isochoric MD. An impact velocity of 2 km/s is added to the thermal velocities to all the atoms in the projectile along [001] in the direction of the target. Adiabatic MD is used to simulate the impact and subsequent expansion. All atomic interactions are described using an EAM potential developed by Fellinger et al. [1] and downloaded from OpenKIM [2]. [1] Fellinger MR, Park H, Wilkins JW. Force-matched embedded-atom method potential for niobium. Physical Review B. 2010Apr;81(14):144119. doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.81.144119 [2] https://doi.org/10.25950/befb2eea.

result.sanitized_script:
units metal
atom_style atomic
boundary p p s
lattice bcc 3.3079 orient x 1 0 0 orient y 0 1 0 orient z 0 0 1
region simbox block 0 20 0 20 -10 80 units lattice
create_box 1 simbox
region rtarget block 0 20 0 20 0 40 units lattice
create_atoms 1 region rtarget
region rproj block 0 20 0 20 44.53459899029596 64.53459899029596 units lattice
create_atoms 1 region rproj
mass 1 92.90638
group target region rtarget
group proj region rproj
pair_style eam/alloy
pair_coeff * * prompt3.potential Nb
velocity all create 300 12345 mom yes rot yes dist gaussian
timestep 0.001
fix nvt_eq all nvt temp 300 300 0.1
thermo 1000
thermo_style custom step temp pe ke etotal press
run 100000
unfix nvt_eq
velocity proj set 0 0 -20 sum yes units box
fix nve_imp all nve
thermo 100
thermo_style custom step temp pe ke etotal press
run 100000

result.text:
Domain review (metal units throughout):

UNITS / VELOCITIES: 2 km/s correctly converted to 20 Å/ps and added with 'sum yes' to thermal velocities of the projectile group along -z toward the target. Correct.

GEOMETRY: BCC Nb lattice a=3.3079 Å matches the Fellinger potential header. Target = 20×20×40 cells (132.32 Å along z, 32000 atoms), projectile = 20×20×20 cells (16000 atoms), gap = 15 Å (1.5 nm). Total 48000 atoms — matches the LAMMPS log. The projectile region was shifted by gap/a in lattice units; because the lattice generator places atoms at integer lattice sites regardless of the region origin, the resulting projectile retains exactly 20 cells of atoms. Correct.

BOUNDARIES: 'p p s' implements periodic along [100]/[010] and shrink-wrapped (free) along [001] as required. The simbox provides 10 lattice units of vacuum below and ~16 above the projectile so atoms do not exit the box on contact.

POTENTIAL: pair_style eam/alloy with the setfl-format prompt3.potential (Fellinger 2010, Nb BCC) is appropriate. Mass 92.90638 matches Nb.

EQUILIBRATION: NVT at 300 K, Tdamp = 0.1 ps (standard for metal units), 100 ps total (100000 × 1 fs). 'mom yes rot yes' on velocity create removes COM drift, which is the correct ordering — the impact velocity is added afterward, deliberately giving the projectile net momentum.

ADIABATIC IMPACT: fix nve on all atoms after impact velocity is set. Correct for shock/spall.

[NOTE] No dump command is included; for actual spall analysis the user will want trajectory output (e.g., dump custom every 100 fs with c_csym or c_stress/atom) to detect void nucleation. Not strictly required by the prompt, but typical for this workflow.

[NOTE] Impact run of 100 ps. Shock transit through the 132 Å target at ~5 km/s ≈ 26 ps; reflection plus spall opening adds another 30–60 ps. 100 ps should capture the spall event but is on the short side if the user wants to observe void coalescence — increasing to 150–200 ps is worth considering.

[NOTE] Tdamp=0.1 ps is fine, but the equilibration is run on the entire system including the projectile sitting in vacuum — the projectile's two free surfaces may contribute slightly more thermal noise; this is physical and not a script bug.

No physical-correctness warnings.
